lots.guide_summary: A$448 to A$718 from the two asks I opened, both Norwegian private listings in working or better condition, one with a flight case. All ASKING, with no sold or unsold results found anywhere. Unverified snippet leads range from A$172 (Reverb low) to A$574. A heavy desk in Australia with a missing cap and unknown function is likely worth well below these, perhaps A$150 to A$350. Rates: 1 NOK = 0.14949 AUD, 1 USD = 1.4352, 1 EUR = 1.6297 (frankfurter 2026-09-30, as supplied by the researcher).
lots.working: No SOLD evidence at all, so both maximums are 0. Asking prices are for tested units overseas and cannot set a bid.
lots.confidence_reason: Model badge read clearly, but the only evidence is asking prices (2 opened, the rest snippet only), and it is untested.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged badges read 'MACKIE ... 4-BUS MIXING CONSOLE' (small print partly legible) and 'SR24.4' and 'VLZ Very Low Impedance Design'. That is the original SR24.4 VLZ, not the VLZ Pro the researcher named (the Pro badge reads VLZ PRO). Fader strip enlarged: channel 3 has no fader cap, but the slot looks intact, so the 'slider missing' is probably just the cap, a cheap part. The other 23 channel faders, sub faders and main fader all have caps. The surface is dusty but no knobs are visibly missing. Rear panel and power not shown.
lots.condition: Cosmetically fair and dusty. One fader cap missing (channel 3). Untested, and the scratchy pots and faders typical of old desks are unknown. No case.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is it only the fader cap on channel 3 that is missing, or the whole fader? Has it been powered up (the SR24.4 has a built-in supply), is the power lead included, and are any channels dead or crackly?
lots.dropped_entries: AudioFanzine 'US$361 market value' dropped: it is a site estimate flagged as outdated, for the VLZ Pro, and not a sale or a listing.
